Fit the covariate gate by EM

Source: R/gate.R
fit_gate.Rd

Combines the prior state probability \(\pi_i(\gamma) = \mathrm{expit} (x_i^\top \gamma)\) with the two class likelihoods to form the posterior responsibility $$w_i(\gamma) = \frac{\pi_i L_{i1}}{\pi_i L_{i1} + (1-\pi_i) L_{i0}},$$ then refits \(\gamma\) by logistic regression using \(w_i\) as a fractional outcome, iterating to convergence. A participant whose trajectory does not discriminate the states keeps a responsibility close to the gate probability and contributes at that weight rather than being forced into a class.

Usage

fit_gate(l1, l0, X, firth = FALSE, maxit = 2000L, tol = 1e-11)

Arguments

l1, l0

Log class likelihoods for state 1 and state 0, one per participant. See class_loglik().

X

Gate design matrix, one row per participant, including an intercept column.

firth

Use the Jeffreys-penalised score of Firth (1993). Recommended when any fitted probability approaches zero or one, which is routine with few participants per covariate level.

maxit, tol

Iteration controls.

Value

An object of class mbmm_gate: gamma, the observed-data loglik, the responsibilities w, fitted probabilities pi, and, when firth = TRUE, the penalised objective \(\ell + \tfrac12 \log |X^\top W X|\).

References

Firth D (1993). Bias reduction of maximum likelihood estimates. Biometrika 80, 27-38.

See also

gate_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 60; x <- rnorm(n); X <- cbind(1, x)
l1 <- rnorm(n, 1); l0 <- rnorm(n)
fit_gate(l1, l0, X)$gamma
#>                       x 
#> 24.76340468 -0.03506096
